clue.text: Many refuse to speed

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword stand-in for a large number
ash is burnt waste, refuse from a fire

explanation.surface: Lots of people won't break the speed limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a verb (decline) but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to rush or hurry, and as a noun a dash is a quick burst of pace.

clue.text: Flotsam and jetsam?

parts.note: rubbish floating in or washed up from the sea can be thought of as litter from the deep, the deep being a poetic word for the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: The real phrase is a poultry-keeping term: a thick bed of straw and droppings left to build up on a henhouse floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means rubbish from the ocean, which is what floating wreckage and cargo are.

clue.text: Poles, forever short, are derisory

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
N stands for the North Pole

indicators.note: short here means losing a letter, as in the poetic contraction e'er

parts.note: ever means forever

explanation.surface: Polish people, never quite lasting, are scornful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means the compass points; 'short' cuts V to give the poetic E'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneer is to show contempt, which is what being derisory means.

clue.text: Real estate apt to have strings attached

parts.note: apt means fitting, proper
ties are cords or strings used to fasten things

explanation.surface: A house sale that may come with conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strings attached' suggests conditions on a deal, but the ties are simply joined after PROPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Properties are buildings and land owned, the holdings that make up real estate.

clue.text: The abuse of some fence

definitions.meaning: a barrier of bars, a kind of fence

explanation.definitionFit: Railing means scolding loudly (abuse) and also a barrier of rails (a type of fence).

clue.text: Is able to turn round in long boat

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the yearning word

parts.note: to pine is to long for something

indicators.note: turn round tells us the word for being able is read backwards

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: Someone who can turn about inside a lengthy vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective describing the boat but is the verb, to yearn; 'turn round' makes NAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnace is a small ship's boat, so it is an example of a boat.

clue.text: Laughing train-wrecker

indicators.note: a wrecker smashes things up, so the letters of train are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A saboteur of railways chuckling at the derailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecker' scrambles TRAIN into the answer, a literary word from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Riant is a literary adjective meaning smiling or cheerful, from the French for mirthful.

clue.text: To do without preparation is better all round

indicators.note: all round says the word for better goes around is

parts.note: to better something is to improve it

explanation.surface: Winging it is better in every way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' looks like an adverb meaning in every way, but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to perform or make something on the spot, unrehearsed.

clue.text: No choice fish!

explanation.definitionFit: Sole means the only one (no choice) and also names a flatfish.

clue.text: A girl's name of Stuart times

definitions.meaning: ... describes the reigns of Charles I and II, kings of the Stuart dynasty, from Latin Carolus

explanation.walkthrough: The Stuarts were the royal house of Scotland and England in the 1600s; Charles is Carolus in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name and also an adjective for the era of King Charles in the Stuart period.

clue.text: Live on tea, maybe, showing a certain loftiness

indicators.note: maybe suggests these words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone surviving on cups of tea looks rather superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges LIVEONTEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation means height or a raised position, and also nobility of style.

clue.text: A Northerner's comeback causing shock

indicators.note: comeback means the northerner's word comes back, read right to left

parts.note: a Lapp is a person from Lapland in the far north of Europe

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian's retort causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' looks like a retort, but signals PPAL; Lapland spans the far north of Scandinavia and Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to dismay or horrify, to shock.

clue.text: Musicians' go-slow movement

parts.note: reads like industrial action by an orchestra, but describes a piece of music marked to be played slowly

explanation.walkthrough: A go-slow is a British form of workers' protest, deliberately working slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is an Italian tempo marking for a very slow, broad pace, and a movement in that tempo.

clue.text: Idleness indeed!

definitions.meaning: split as in deed: in a deed, doing something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means doing nothing, yet split into two words it means busy at work, which is literally being in deed.

clue.text: Dicky sits eating eggs

indicators.note: dicky is old slang for faulty or shaky, so the letters are unsound and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rickety bird sits feeding on its clutch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' looks like a container signal but is part of the anagram pool; dicky is British slang for unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs is the verb, as in eggs on: urges or incites someone to act.

clue.text: Checking new setting

indicators.note: new means the letters of setting are made into a fresh form

explanation.surface: Inspecting a fresh stage set or jewel mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SETTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Testing means trying something out or examining it, which is checking.

clue.text: Taking fruit to fill up, figure should be trim

indicators.note: to fill up says the fruit goes inside the word for figure

parts.note: shape means figure, form
hips are the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: Eating fruit fills you out, but a good figure should be slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit' suggests something sweet, but rose hips are meant; 'to fill up' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and in good order, which is trim.

clue.text: Feeling a book turned one on

indicators.note: turned means the word for a book faces the other way

parts.note: a tome is a book, especially a large one
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A novel turned a reader on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses TOME to EMOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling such as joy or anger.

clue.text: Open bag up inside, being far from bright

indicators.note: inside puts the reversed bag within the word for open

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden

indicators.note: up, in a down entry, means the word for bag is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch in an animal or plant

explanation.surface: Unzip the bag and look within: it is dim in there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open bag' looks like an instruction to unzip something; 'up' in a down clue turns the bag word to CAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is cloudy and dull, which is far from bright.

clue.text: There's a bit of a problem in entertaining the distinguished

indicators.note: a bit of says the answer is a stretch of letters sitting within the following words

explanation.surface: A slight problem when hosting important guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'problEM IN ENTertaining'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means famous and respected in a field, which is distinguished.

clue.text: Note a number tucked into appropriate snack

indicators.note: tucked into puts the note, a and the number inside the word for appropriate

parts.note: to appropriate is to take for oneself
E is a musical note
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A banknote and figures slipped into a fitting light meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' is a verb here, not an adjective; 'tucked into' puts E, A and C inside TAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a light sweet bun, usually toasted and buttered, eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Ostensible reason for a foreword?

definitions.meaning: a stated excuse that hides the real motive

explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false excuse; split, it describes what comes before a book's text, as a foreword does.

clue.text: Bore down on a leading journalist

definitions.meaning: split as ..., short for a press editor, a senior journalist

explanation.definitionFit: Pressed means pushed down upon; split, it gives a newspaper editor, the journalist leading the paper.

clue.text: A letter making silly sap quite cross

indicators.note: silly means the letters of sap are muddled

parts.note: irate means angry, quite cross

explanation.surface: A note written to make a foolish twit furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges SAP to ASP. In phonetics an aspirate is the H sound, so the letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirate is a breathed sound, and in particular the letter H that represents it.

clue.text: A little place built entirely of tiles

indicators.note: built entirely of says the answer is constructed from these letters and nothing else

explanation.surface: A small house made only of tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built entirely of' rearranges TILES.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a small island, a little piece of land.

clue.text: The Conservative leader, taking a breather, held on

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Conservative

parts.note: a lung is an organ of breathing

explanation.surface: The Tory leader, pausing for breath, clung to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a breather' looks like a rest, but is the breathing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung means held tightly, gripped, held on.

clue.text: The practice of the top-drawer philosopher

parts.note: U is a British label for upper-class ..., and top-drawer means upper-class
a sage is a wise thinker

explanation.surface: The habits of an upper-class thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class comes from a 1950s British essay that sorted words into U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is habitual practice or custom.

clue.text: As is written repeatedly, she was once highly respected

indicators.note: written repeatedly means the little word is set down twice in a row

explanation.surface: As the record says again and again, she was revered.
explanation.walkthrough: Isis was a goddess of ancient Egypt; Isis is also the name of the Thames at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a major goddess of ancient Egypt, worshipped and revered.

clue.text: A way everybody can ensure a good seat at the theatre

definitions.text: a good seat at the theatre

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A method for securing everyone a fine spot in the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: In British theatres the stalls are the seats on the ground floor near the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stall is a seat on the main floor of a theatre, among the best placed.

clue.text: The simpleton is French so finds a supporter

parts.note: an ass is a fool
tant is French for so, so much

explanation.surface: The fool is French, so he finds a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French so' looks like a nationality and a link, but asks for the French word for so.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is a helper, someone who supports another's work.

clue.text: Bed-linen gets all twisted — in knots

parts.note: a sheet is a piece of bed-linen
bends means turns out of shape, gets twisted

explanation.surface: The bedclothes end up in a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: A sheet bend is a sailor's knot for joining two ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheet bends are a type of knot used to tie two lines together.

clue.text: The head needs a lot of water

definitions.meaning: Loch ... is a large lake in Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ness means a headland or promontory, and Loch Ness is a huge Scottish lake.
